transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (CS), Marta Reyes (Skyline Head of ML), Tom Chen (Skyline Product), Arjun Patel (Skyline Infra), Sophia Li (Skyline DS)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect): Redwood demo of Evaluate/Quality-monitoring; focused on how to run prompt sets, set regression alert thresholds, and run A/B experiments via Console and API. Action items: share pricing, set up eval project, schedule bench.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — I'm Jordan, AE, and Priya is our SE who'll show the Console and the eval flow.
[00:12] Marta: Hi, Marta here — thanks, excited. We have a lot to cover; our top ask is to detect regressions when we change models or quantize.
[00:20] Priya: Great. Outline for today: quick API demo, then Console walkthrough of Evaluate/Quality monitoring, how prompt sets map to regression alerts, and finally A/B comparisons and Optimize suggestions. We'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:35] Tom: Timeline wise we want a pilot in the next 2-3 weeks if possible. Budget and legal signoffs are another thread.
[00:44] Jordan: Totally. We'll discuss pilot SKUs and security docs as next steps.

--- API demo / quick concepts ---
[01:05] Priya: I'll start with the API — sending prompt sets in batch, how to store ground truth labels, and our evaluation endpoints for metrics like exact match, BLEU, and custom scoring. Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/evals -d '{"prompt_set_id":"ps-123"}' — apologies if auto-transcript mangles JSON.
[01:40] Sophia: Do you support multiple metrics per prompt? We want both semantic similarity and rule-based checks.
[01:47] Priya: Yes, you can attach multiple metrics per eval; we also let you bring your own metric hooks via a small lambda-style runner in the private deployment.
[01:58] Arjun: How do you handle tokenization differences across model variants? That affects scoring for token-level metrics.
[02:08] Priya: Good point — our eval runner normalizes using model-specific tokenizers and records tokenizer metadata per run; you can see per-model token counts in the Console.

--- Console walkthrough: prompt sets, dashboards ---
[03:10] Priya: Switching to the Console — here's the Eval dashboard. You can create prompt sets by uploading CSVs or via API. You can tag prompts with scenario, priority, and expected output.
[03:40] Marta: Can we version prompt sets? We iterate often.
[03:46] Priya: Yes, every prompt set has versions; you can pin a prompt set to an alert policy or a rollout.
[04:02] Tom: Show us how regression alerts look; we want to catch both quality drop and latency regressions.
[04:10] Priya: Sure. Alerts can be metric-based (e.g. pass rate drops 3% absolute), or threshold-based on p95 latency. You can also create composite alerts — for example, quality drop AND error-rate spike.
[04:32] Jordan: Many customers tie alerts to rollback policies so that a canary failing eval triggers auto-fallback to the previous model.
[04:42] Sophia: That rollback — is it supported in Hosted and Dedicated?
[04:47] Priya: Yes, rollback policies can be configured across hosted and dedicated. For Private, we provide the same control plane APIs; customers run the control plane in VPC.

[05:10] Marta: How do you handle false positives? Sometimes a prompt set has nondeterministic outputs.
[05:18] Priya: We recommend grouping stochastic prompts separately and use statistical tests across windows; Redwood's console shows confidence intervals and you can set alert sensitivity. Also we support sampling the actual generations for human review.

--- Prompt sets and evaluation details ---
[06:00] Priya: Example: we uploaded three prompt sets — checkout_flow, returns_flow, recommendations — each with ground truth or expected patterns. You can run an eval across multiple model variants and see delta tables.
[06:20] Jordan: And the A/B comparison?
[06:24] Priya: In the A/B flow you define traffic split, run evals in parallel, and Redwood produces per-cohort metrics plus significance tests. You can also run batch offline A/B comparisons using the eval runner with your stored requests.
[06:45] Tom: Are there visualizations for human-in-the-loop review? We want to quickly triage failing prompts.
[06:52] Priya: Yes — the Console surfaces failing prompts, with example generations side-by-side, diff highlights, and tags so your reviewers can triage and add notes.

--- Discussion: regression alerts, thresholds, and Ops integration ---
[08:05] Arjun: From infra perspective we need audit logs for all eval runs and RBAC so only certain personas can trigger rollouts.
[08:12] Jordan: Redwood supports audit logs and detailed event traces. Priya, quick note on SSO?
[08:18] Priya: We have SAML SSO + SCIM, role mappings, and audit export to your SIEM. Also KMS integrations for private deployments — we support customer-managed keys.
[08:32] Marta: Good. Data residency? We need logs retained in EU for some cohorts.
[08:38] Priya: You can scope eval projects to specific regions; retention policies are configurable per project for Console-based storage.

--- A/B comparisons and statistical rigor ---
[09:20] Priya: For A/B we run bootstrap significance tests by default; you can choose t-tests or nonparametric tests. We report p-values, confidence intervals, and minimum detectable effect given sample size.
[09:42] Sophia: Nice — can we attach business KPIs for lift measurement?
[09:47] Priya: Yes, you can map model metrics to business KPIs and Redwood will compute per-variant KPI estimates if you provide conversion tags.

--- Optimize suggestions: quantization and batching ---
[11:05] Priya: The Optimize tab suggests quantization profiles and batching configs based on your traffic. For a specific prompt set we can recommend per-model quantization (e.g., 4-bit QAT vs int8) and estimate token cost savings and expected quality delta.
[11:28] Marta: We run a lot of small prompts — batching might not help. How does Redwood handle mixed workloads?
[11:35] Priya: We have adaptive batching: short prompts can be grouped separately; the runtime uses workload-aware policies to keep latency SLOs while batching. The Console shows simulated latency/cost curves for different batch sizes.

--- Live demo: uploading Skyline prompt set and running an eval ---
[13:00] Priya: Ok I'm uploading the CSV Marta shared earlier. Upload complete — creating eval run against model variants: gptx-3-redwood, gptx-3-redwood-quant4 and a baseline open model.
[13:28] Jordan: While that runs, can you show the diff view?
[13:31] Priya: Here's the diff — you can see per-prompt pass/fail, metric deltas, and an overall regression score. Note some transcribed names may show as g p t x in the UI — sometimes tokenization tags get rendered oddly in auto transcripts.
[14:02] Sophia: I see several fails on the returns_flow — can we group by intent?
[14:08] Priya: Yep, tag by scenario and filter. Also you can create a dynamic alert that watches the returns_flow pass rate and triggers if it drops 2% week-over-week.

[15:00] Tom: For the pilot we'd like a nightly run and an immediate alert channel to Slack, plus the option to create a human-review queue. Is that doable?
[15:10] Priya: Totally. We have Slack webhook integrations and a built-in review queue that routes samples to reviewers; you can set thresholds for automatic escalation.

--- Security and compliance questions ---
[17:05] Arjun: For Dedicated/Private we need KMS, HSM options, and audit retention of 1 year. Also do you support bringing your own keys?
[17:15] Priya: Yes, BYOK via cloud KMS, and HSM integration for on-prem. Audit logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM with configurable retention. We'll share the security pack in the follow-up.

--- Pricing and pilot structure ---
[19:00] Jordan: For pilots we typically do a 30-day eval with reserved capacity for the bench runs plus hosted eval access; we'll send a pilot SKU. Pilot includes one SE bench session.
[19:20] Marta: Sounds good; budget signoff on our side is likely by next Friday.

--- Q&A and edge cases ---
[22:10] Sophia: How do you handle hallucination scoring? We need to run rule-based checks against a knowledge base.
[22:18] Priya: You can attach custom verifiers that call your KB; results are returned as metrics. We also support embedding-based similarity checks.
[22:35] Tom: Any limitations on prompt set size? We have ~20k prompts for some flows.
[22:42] Priya: The Console and API support large prompt sets; for very large corpora we recommend batch uploads and using the eval runner in Dedicated/Private for throughput.

--- Closing, recap, and next steps ---
[26:00] Jordan: Quick recap: we'll send pricing and pilot details, Priya will provision the eval project in Console and upload the Skyline prompt set, Arjun will give sample traffic profiles, and Sophia will share the 2 canonical prompt sets. We'll follow up with a bench run week of 2025-10-20.
[26:24] Marta: Perfect. Please include SOC 2 docs and KMS/HSM notes in the follow-up.
[26:35] Liam: I'll attach the deck and a short how-to for reviewers; link posted in chat: https://tinyurl.com/rwd-eval-deck
[26:46] Jordan: Thanks everyone.
[26:50] Marta: Thanks.

(Transcript continues with some cross-talk and shorter clarifications; auto-transcript artifacts present: occasional mis-attributed speakers and tokenization of model names.)

End of transcript.
